findings.title: Global CSRF check blocks all mutating requests before route-specific parsing or exemptions
findings.evidence: The middleware is installed application-wide with 'app.use(csrfProtection);', and it rejects every non-safe method unless the 'x-csrf-token' header matches. This is a reachable regression for any existing POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE endpoint in this app that is intended for non-browser/API clients, webhooks, or other callers that do not send this header.
findings.recommendation: Apply CSRF protection only to browser session-backed routes that need it, or add explicit exemptions for API/webhook endpoints and document the required token flow before enabling it globally.

findings.title: Middleware denies all mutating requests when no session token has been established
findings.evidence: The check compares the request header against 'req.session?.csrfToken' and returns 403 on mismatch, but this file only comments that session middleware is assumed and does not establish or initialize a CSRF token anywhere in the request path shown here. In any supported deployment where session setup is absent, misordered, or does not populate 'csrfToken', every POST to '/profile' and '/transfer' will be rejected.
findings.recommendation: Ensure session middleware and CSRF token generation run before this middleware, or guard startup/configuration so the app fails fast instead of silently rejecting all mutating requests when 'req.session.csrfToken' is unavailable.
